title: Protocol for Preparing Drosophila Genomic DNA for Genome Assemblies
author: Sperling, Fabian, et al.
materials: KAPA HyperPrep kits for NGS DNA library prep
NEBNext Ultra II DNA library prep kit

This is a modified protocol for high molecular DNA isolation with QIAGEN Genomic-tips.3.Disrupt cells.a.Prepare the lysis buffer by adding 19 μL RNase A to 9.5 mL of Buffer G2.i.Mix and setting aside.b.Place 60 mg of sample (30–60 flies) in a 1.5 mL tube.i.Place 1.5 mL tube with the flies in liquid Nitrogen (N2).Note: Use tongs.ii.Place pestle tip in liquid N2. Troubleshooting 3.iii.While the bottom of the tube is in contact (use tongs) with the N2 slowly manually grind the flies until broken up.iv.Blend the broken-up flies with a handheld electric pestle mixer until a fine powder.Note: For the best results the tube must remain partially submerged in the N2 in order to prevent condensation from forming on the sample.4.Extract and concentrate DNA.a.Add 240 μL of lysis buffer to the 1.5 mL tube containing the fly powder and then transfer the lysis-fly solution into a 15 mL tube (on ice).i.Repeat 3 times to ensure that all the material is transferred.ii.Add the remaining lysis buffer to the tube.b.Immediately vortex for 5 s.c.Incubate lysate at 37°C for 1 h, gently inverting tube after 30 min.d.Digest proteini.Add 500 μL QIAGEN Proteinase K and gently invert the tube 5 times.ii.Incubate at 50°C for 2 h and gently inverting the tube 5 times after 1 h.iii.10 min before the end of the lysis incubation time, prepare a Genomic-tip by equilibrating it with 4 mL Buffer QBT.e.Isolate DNA.i.Vortex the lysed sample for 5–10 s at maximum speed.ii.Gently pour the sample into five 2 mL tubes.iii.Centrifuge at 5,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.iv.Immediately after the centrifugation pour the samples on the equilibrated Genomic-tip.v.Wash twice with 7.5 mL Buffer QC.vi.Pre-warm 5 mL Buffer QF to 50°C.vii.Eluted DNA with the 5 mL warm Buffer QF into a 50 mL tube.f.Concentrate DNA.i.Add 3.5 mL isopropanol to the sample.ii.Gently invert 10–20 times.iii.Pour sample into 2.0 mL tubes and centrifuged immediately at 10,000 × g for 30 min at 4°C.iv.Decant supernatant off and washed the pellet twice with 1 mL cold 70% ethanol.v.Centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.vi.Air dry DNA for 5–10 min.vii.Re-suspend in 50 μL elution buffer.viii.Incubate at 37°C for 30–60 min and leave in the fridge for 16 h (overnight).CRITICAL: It is important to not pipette the DNA, when possible, pour the DNA-containing liquid over to new vessels or use wide-bore, low-bind pipette tips.CRITICAL: Use tongs when working with samples proximal to N2.

Quality control is the most important part of high molecular weight DNA preparation. It is important to start with high-quality DNA because the library preparation will result in some DNA fragmentation.5.DNA concentration NanoDrop.a.Gently mix DNA sample.b.Measure the concentration with NanoDrop.Note: The A260/280 and A260/230 are important because they can help indicated if there are impurities, particularly residual phenol that may interfere with the sequencing. The values should be approximately A260/280 1.80 and A260/230 should be 2.0–2.2 (see the Thermo Fisher Scientific NanoDrop T042-TECHNICAL BULLETIN).6.DNA concentration using Qubit.a.Obtain the DNA concentration using the standard Qubit protocol.Note: Make sure to perform the calibration.b.The concentration should be in a similar range to the NanoDrop.Note: If the concentration measurements are off by over 0.5-fold then there may be impurities in your sample that can interfere with Nanopore sequencing.7.Pulse-field gel electrophoresis, with Pippin Pulse.a.Cast 0.75% high strength agarose gel.i.0.825 g of agarose in 0.5% KBB buffer (diluted from 10× KBB stock with ultra-pure water).Note: TBE buffer can also be used, see Pippin Pulse User Manual.b.Prepare samples.i.100 ng of DNA in 10 μL of elution buffer with 2 μL of loading buffer.c.Place gel with the correct orientation in tank, fill with 0.5% KKB.d.Load 10 μL samples and 5 Kb ladder at both ends of the gel.e.Run on the program for 5–80 Kb of DNA at 75 V for 15 h (overnight).f.Soak gel in ethidium bromide for 30 min.g.Image gel.Note: This step will indicate how fragmented the DNA is and is important for decided to go forward with the sequencing.CRITICAL: Caution when handling ethidium bromide, it is a potential carcinogen.

A common step in preparing genome assemblies is polishing the assembly with short-read genome data produced using another method. Hi-C is most often used for polishing because it will give a better chromosome-level assembly. However, for Drosophila it is possible to use short-read libraries since the chromosome arms are conserved.21,22,23,24 Hi-C is still recommended for obtaining better resolution of the non-coding regions of Drosophila genomes. Here we use Illumina sequencing technology to sequence a whole genome DNA preparation in combination with transcriptomics data to polish the genome assembly. The same respective methods to prepare genomic DNA for long-read sequencing were used for the short-read DNA preparation. However, for the short-read library preparation only a single fly was used for the genomic DNA preparation.11.Library preparation can be done with almost any commercially available kit.Note: We used the KAPA HyperPrep Kits for NGS DNA Library Prep by Roche for the parthenogenetic genomes and the NEBNext Ultra II DNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina by New England Biolabs for the sexually reproducing genome.a.Follow the manufactures protocol in preparing the libraries.12.Library quality control (the same as for high molecular weight DNA preparation).a.Quantify concentration using NanoDrop.b.Quantify concentration using Qubit.c.Check the quality of the library Agilent TapeStation or Agilent Bioanalyzer (Figure 2)Figure 2Short-read D. mercatorum genome library quality control(A) Bioanalyzer results for the parthenogenetic genome library. There is a single sample peak along with the lower and upper markers. The average size of the library is 635 bp.(B) TapeStation results for the sexually reproducing genome library. There is a single sample peak along with the lower and upper markers. The average size of the library is 513 bp.Note: We recommend using the TapeStation if possible due to the ease of use and longer lifetime of the reagents.13.Sequencing can be done on any of the Illumina platforms.Note: We used both the MiSeq and the NovaSeq.Note: For our experiments we also polished the genome using transcriptomics data from our cells of interest. This was beneficial for comparison purposed between our genes of interest.
Timing: 5 days – on a high-performance cluster

steps.title: Prepare reagents and handle DNA gently
steps.instruction: Gather low‑bind plastic consumables and wide‑bore pipette tips; avoid vigorous shaking or vortexing of DNA‑containing tubes unless a step explicitly requires it. Perform all phenol‑containing steps in a fume hood with appropriate protective equipment.

steps.title: Phenol extraction of high‑MW DNA (3 days)
steps.instruction: Isolate high molecular weight genomic DNA from 30–60 Drosophila flies using a phenol‑chloroform method with the detailed incubation times, temperatures, and reagent volumes.

substeps.instruction: Dissociate tissue: place 60 mg of flies in a 1.5 mL tube, add 150 µL SDS buffer, homogenize with a handheld electric pestle for 10 s, add 350 µL SDS buffer, invert gently 5×, incubate 37 °C for 4 h (incubation may be 2–16 h).
Eliminate RNA: add 5 µL RNase A (100 mg/mL), invert gently 5×, incubate 50 °C for 2 h without agitation.
Digest protein: add 5 µL Proteinase K (20 mg/mL), invert gently 5×, incubate 37 °C for 2 h without agitation.
First phenol extraction: add 240 µL phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1), mix gently 3 min at 21 °C, centrifuge 12,000 × g 10 min, decant supernatant to a new tube.
Second phenol extraction: repeat the above with 240 µL fresh phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol, mix, centrifuge, decant.
Third chloroform extraction: add 240 µL chloroform (from the same mixture), mix 3 min at 21 °C, centrifuge 12,000 × g 10 min, decant.
Precipitate DNA: add 500 µL −20 °C absolute ethanol, incubate ≥5 min at −20 °C (pause point up to 16 h).
Spool DNA with a bent pipette tip, place pellet in a new tube, add 80 % ethanol, centrifuge 12,000 × g 3 min, decant, dry at 37 °C for ~30 min (do not exceed).
Elute DNA: add 50 µL elution buffer, leave at 21 °C for 16 h (overnight) then store at 4 °C for at least 2 days before QC.
Critical: avoid pipetting the DNA; pour or use wide‑bore low‑bind tips. Phenol is toxic – work in a fume hood and discard orange/red phenol.

steps.title: QIAGEN Genomic‑Tip extraction (2 days)
steps.instruction: Isolate high molecular weight DNA using QIAGEN Genomic‑Tip columns with the specified lysis, protein digestion, binding, washing, and elution steps.

substeps.instruction: Prepare lysis buffer: add 19 µL RNase A to 9.5 mL Buffer G2, mix and set aside.

Freeze and grind flies: place 60 mg (30–60) flies in a 1.5 mL tube, submerge in liquid N₂, grind with pestle tip while keeping tube partially submerged, then blend with electric pestle to a fine powder.

Lysis: add 240 µL lysis buffer to the powder, transfer to a 15 mL tube on ice (repeat 3 times to collect all material), add remaining lysis buffer, vortex 5 s, incubate 37 °C for 1 h, invert gently after 30 min.
Protein digestion: add 500 µL QIAGEN Proteinase K, invert 5×, incubate 50 °C for 2 h, invert again after 1 h.
Equilibrate Genomic‑Tip: add 4 mL Buffer QBT to the tip and let equilibrate.
Load lysate: vortex lysate 5–10 s at max speed, pour into five 2 mL tubes, centrifuge 5,000 × g 10 min at 4 °C, immediately pour each supernatant onto the equilibrated Genomic‑Tip.
Wash tip twice with 7.5 mL Buffer QC.
Elute DNA: pre‑warm 5 mL Buffer QF to 50 °C, elute into a 50 mL tube.

Concentrate DNA: add 3.5 mL isopropanol, invert 10–20×, transfer to 2 mL tubes, centrifuge 10,000 × g 30 min at 4 °C, decant supernatant, wash pellet twice with 1 mL cold 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 10,000 × g 5 min at 4 °C, air‑dry 5–10 min.
Resuspend pellet in 50 µL elution buffer, incubate 37 °C for 30–60 min, then store at 4 °C for 16 h (overnight).
Critical: avoid pipetting DNA; pour or use wide‑bore low‑bind tips. Use tongs when handling liquid N₂.

steps.title: DNA quality control (2 days)
steps.instruction: Assess concentration, purity, and fragment size of the extracted high‑MW DNA.

substeps.instruction: NanoDrop: gently mix the DNA sample, measure concentration, record A260/280 (≈1.80) and A260/230 (2.0–2.2).
Qubit: follow the standard Qubit dsDNA assay protocol, perform calibration, compare concentration to NanoDrop (difference >0.5‑fold indicates impurity).

Pulse‑field gel electrophoresis (Pippin Pulse): cast a 0.75 % agarose gel (0.825 g agarose in 0.5 % KBB buffer); load 100 ng DNA in 10 µL elution buffer + 2 µL loading buffer; run 5–80 kb program at 75 V for 15 h (overnight); soak gel in ethidium bromide 30 min; image gel. Note: handle ethidium bromide with care (carcinogen).

steps.title: Short‑read library prep and QC (2 days)
steps.instruction: Prepare Illumina short‑read libraries from a single fly DNA sample, assess library quality, and sequence.

substeps.instruction: Library preparation: use KAPA HyperPrep Kit (parthenogenetic sample) or NEBNext Ultra II DNA Library Prep Kit (sexually reproducing sample) following the manufacturers’ protocols.
Library QC: quantify library with NanoDrop and Qubit; assess fragment size with Agilent TapeStation or Bioanalyzer (expected average size ≈635 bp for parthenogenetic, ≈513 bp for sexual).
Sequencing: load libraries on an Illumina platform (MiSeq or NovaSeq) and run according to standard Illumina protocols.

steps.title: Genome assembly and polishing (5 days)
steps.instruction: Assemble Nanopore reads, polish with Illumina data, compute assembly metrics, align genomes, and perform k‑mer quality analysis.

substeps.instruction: Assemble Nanopore reads: run wtdbg2 with parameters `-x ont -g 200m -i ../Sample_1.ont.fq.gz -t 24 -fo Sample_1.ont.wtdbg2`, then map reads with minimap2 `-t 24 -ax map-ont -r2k Sample_1.ont.wtdbg2.raw.fa ../Sample_1.ont.fq.gz`, pipe to `samtools sort -@4 > Sample_1.ont.bam`, filter with `samtools view -F 0x900`, and generate consensus with `wtpoa-cns -t 24 -d Sample_1.ont.wtdbg2.raw.fa -i - -fo Sample_1.ont.wtdbg2.cns.fa`. Repeat for Sample_2.

Polish with Illumina reads: align Illumina reads to the draft assembly using `bwa mem -t 48 Sample_1.ont.wtdbg2.cns.fa Sample_1/illumina/Sample_1.s_1.r_1.fq.gz Sample_1/illumina/Sample_1.s_1.r_2.fq.gz > Sample_1.illumina.sam`; convert to BAM `samtools view -b Sample_1.illumina.sam > Sample_1.illumina.raw.bam`; sort with `sambamba sort -t 48 Sample_1.illumina.raw.bam`; remove intermediate files.

Variant calling: for each contig, run `freebayes -f Sample_1.ont.wtdbg2.cns.fa --region <contig> Sample_1.illumina.raw.bam | bcftools view --no-version -Ob -o - > calls/<contig>.polish1.bcf`. Concatenate BCFs with `bcftools concat -nf concat_list.txt | bcftools view -Ou -e 'type="ref"' | bcftools norm -Ob -f Sample_1.ont.wtdbg2.cns.fa -o Sample_1.illumina.bcf` (list generated by `cat Sample_1.ont.wtdbg2.cns.fa.fai | cut -f1 > concat_list.txt`).
Apply polishing: `bcftools consensus -I 'QUAL>1 && (GT="AA" || GT="Aa")' -H la -f Sample_1.ont.wtdbg2.cns.fa Sample_1.illumina.bcf > Sample_1.ont.wtdbg2.cns.polish.fa`.

Compute assembly statistics: use `samtools coverage Sample_1.ont.bam > Sample_1.ont.bam.samtools_coverage.txt` and `samtools coverage -w 160 Sample_1.ont.bam > Sample_1.ont.bam.samtools_coverage.asciiart.txt` to obtain NG50, coverage, etc.

Align assemblies: compress with `fastix -p "Sample_1#" Sample_1.ont.wtdbg2.cns.polish.fa | bgzip -@24 > Sample_1.fa.gz && samtools faidx Sample_1.fa.gz`; repeat for Sample_2 and D. melanogaster (GCF_000001215.4_Release_6_plus_ISO1_MT_genomic.fna). Run wfmash `wfmash -p 70 -t 48 dmel6.fa.gz Sample_1.fa.gz > dmel6_vs_Sample_1.paf.gz` and analogous commands for other pairwise comparisons.

Coverage & heterozygosity: use `samtools view -b Sample_1.ont.sam | samtools sort -@24 -o Sample_1.ont.bam.1 && samtools index Sample_1.ont.bam.1` then `samtools coverage Sample_1.ont.bam > Sample_1.ont.bam.samtools_coverage.txt`. For Illumina BAMs, sort with `sambamba`, call variants with `freebayes`, filter SNPs with `vcfwave | vcffilter -f 'TYPE = snp'` and compute heterozygosity as described.

Merqury k‑mer analysis: count 19‑mers with `meryl k=19 count output Sample_1.illumina.fastq.meryl Sample_1.illumina.fastq`; run `merqury.sh Sample_1.illumina.fastq.meryl Sample_1.fa Sample_1.merqury`; plot spectra using the provided R code (ggplot of k‑mer multiplicity).
